title: Rora loss produces a thalamic excitability and synaptic liability program distinct from weak Rorb/Rorc paralog responses
exact_observed_result: Rora loss drove a strong 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut program marked by repression of Prkcg, Adgrb1, Grin2c, Kcnc2, Gabra4, Gabrd, Gria2, and Sema7a with a smaller induced component, while Rorb and Rorc were weak or inactive in the same thalamic context.
biological_interpretation: ROR-alpha has a selective thalamic excitability and synaptic-output role in this acute neuronal assay that is not recapitulated by lowering the ROR paralogs Rorb or Rorc.

source_findings.direction: 151 selective response; no FDR-significant genes in 21 other Rora tests
source_findings.summary: Rora perturbation produced a strong FDR-significant program only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while 21 other assayed cell classes were transcriptionally quiet at FDR<0.05.
source_findings.why_it_matters: RORA is broadly expressed in neurons, but the dataset points to a sharply restricted thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic dependency that extends prior RORalpha thalamic-development biology into a perturbational thalamic single-cell context.
source_findings.cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
source_findings.main_caveats: Direct Rora mRNA reduction was nominal rather than FDR-significant, and some silent classes had small n_pert counts.

source_findings.summary: Rora was not interchangeable with its ROR-family paralogs Rorb or Rorc in the responsive thalamic class.
source_findings.why_it_matters: RORA, RORB, and RORC share RORE DNA-recognition logic, yet only Rora created a broad 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature; this argues that the hit is a RORA-specific dependency rather than a generic consequence of perturbing any ROR nuclear receptor.
source_findings.main_caveats: Rorb target engagement was only nominal and Rorc target engagement was not detected, so lack of response could partly reflect ineffective or low-expression perturbation.

source_findings.summary: Rorc did not phenocopy the ROR-family paralog Rora in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
source_findings.why_it_matters: The thalamic class produced a strong Rora program despite a same-family Rorc perturbation with more perturbed cells, arguing against simple interchangeability of ROR-family factors in this neuronal context.
source_findings.main_caveats: Rorc target engagement was poor; the contrast may combine biology with different guide efficacy or baseline expression.

source_findings.summary: Rora loss engaged only a narrow slice of the curated circadian circuit in 151 cells: Nr1d1 and Cry2 fell, but Arntl/Bmal1, Dbp, Clock, Nr1d2, Tef, Cry1, Per2, and Per3 did not pass FDR.
source_findings.why_it_matters: Canonical RORA biology predicts RORE-mediated clock regulation, including BMAL1 activation; the thalamic Perturb-seq result shows that the clock edge most visible after Rora perturbation is Nr1d1/Cry2 loss rather than wholesale BMAL1-CLOCK oscillator collapse.
source_findings.main_caveats: The experiment is not a circadian time course, and absence of FDR signal for Arntl or Dbp at one sampling context does not exclude rhythmic regulation.

source_findings.summary: Rorb mRNA depletion was concentrated in L4-5 IT cortical neurons but did not produce significant downstream genes.
source_findings.why_it_matters: The engaged cell class corresponds to the best-established cortical RORβ context, yet the weak downstream program suggests that acute postnatal perturbation does not replay developmental layer-4 RORβ biology in this dataset.
source_findings.main_caveats: Rorb target transcript FDR was 0.404 and Acin1/Camk4 were the only rows at FDR 0.136; no row crossed 5% FDR.

source_findings.summary: RORE-linked clock and lipid/steroid genes showed only nominal, uncoordinated tails after Rorc perturbation.
source_findings.why_it_matters: RORC can regulate peripheral circadian and metabolic transcription, but those known target families were not detectably organized by Rorc in the assayed brain cell types.
source_findings.main_caveats: The dataset measured an acute perturbation in broad brain classes, whereas much RORC clock and metabolic biology was defined in peripheral tissues or synchronized bulk assays.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: Rora target transcript was measured in all 22 Rora-perturbed cell-type tests; matched perturbation counts ranged from 28 to 139 cells and controls from 3465 to 23679 cells. The Rora logFC was negative in 17/22 tests, nominal p<0.05 in 2/22 tests, and FDR<0.05 in 0/22 tests.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: Across measured contexts, direct Rora transcript depletion was generally weak and did not pass FDR despite guide assignment to Rora.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: 139 perturbed cells versus 23679 controls; 17259 genes tested; 278 genes FDR<0.05, 363 genes FDR<0.1, and 1254 genes nominal p<0.05. The FDR<0.05 genes comprised 176 negative-score and 102 positive-score genes; Rora itself had score -2.696, logFC -0.342, p=0.00702, FDR=0.218.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: The only Rora perturbation with a large FDR-significant response occurred in the thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic class.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: The 21 non-151 Rora tests each had 0 genes at FDR<0.05. The smallest outside-151 FDR values were Car4 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, FDR=0.0762; Ambra1 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, FDR=0.0926; and Dzip3 in 046 CTX-CGE GABA, FDR=0.134.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: No other assayed cell class crossed the dataset FDR threshold for Rora.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: 91 perturbed cells versus 13710 controls; Rora score -2.396, logFC -0.755, p=0.0166, FDR=1.0; 0 genes FDR<0.05 and minimum non-target FDR=1.0.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: Pvalb GABA cells showed nominal Rora transcript reduction but no FDR-significant downstream response.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: Rora had 278 genes FDR<0.05 with 139 perturbed cells. Rorb had 162 perturbed cells, its own transcript logFC -0.373 with p=0.0129 and FDR=1.0, 0 genes FDR<0.05, and Pearson score-correlation to Rora of 0.0366 across 17259 genes. Rorc had 195 perturbed cells, its own transcript p=0.903 and FDR=1.0, 0 genes FDR<0.05, and Pearson correlation to Rora of 0.00725.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: The Rorb and Rorc perturbations did not reproduce the large Rora response in the same thalamic class.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: Rora perturbation: 139 cells, 278 genes at FDR<0.05, min FDR=9.68e-18; top down genes included Prkcg FDR=9.68e-18, Adgrb1 FDR=1.35e-17, and Nr1d1 FDR=5.32e-9. Rorb: 162 cells, 0 genes at FDR<0.05. Rorc: 195 cells, 0 genes at FDR<0.05 and Rorc self p=0.903, FDR=1.0.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: The same thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic class supported a strong Rora response but not a Rorc or Rorb response.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Pearson score correlations with Rorc were Rora r=0.007, Rorb r=0.009, Nr1d1 r=-0.046, and Nr1d2 r=-0.016. Across all shared cell types, the largest absolute Rorc correlation to Rora, Rorb, Nr1d1, or Nr1d2 was |r|=0.095.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: Rorc signatures were effectively uncorrelated with assayed ROR paralogs and REV-ERB neighbors.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: In the Rora 151 signature: Nr1d1 logFC -0.848 FDR=5.32e-09 and Cry2 logFC -0.437 FDR=0.00249 were significant; Arntl logFC -0.383 p=0.0596 FDR=0.750, Npas2 logFC -0.315 p=0.0110 FDR=0.293, Per1 logFC -0.221 p=0.0130 FDR=0.330, and Dbp, Clock, Nr1d2, Tef, Hlf, Cry1, Per2, and Per3 all had FDR=1.0.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: The Rora clock response in 151 cells was selective for a small subset of clock-family transcripts rather than a uniform collapse of the core oscillator.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: Best on-target row: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 118 perturbed versus 15,039 controls, score -3.9734, logFC -0.9010, P=7.085e-05, FDR=0.4044. Next: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 162 versus 23,679, logFC -0.3727, P=0.01294, FDR=1.0. Median target-row P across tested classes=0.732.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: Target-transcript rows for Rorb show nominal depletion in L4-5 IT cortical neurons and weaker nominal depletion in one thalamic glutamatergic class, with no on-target row passing FDR.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: 118 perturbed versus 15,039 controls; Acin1 logFC 0.3402 P=1.25e-05 FDR=0.1363; Camk4 logFC -0.3668 P=1.59e-05 FDR=0.1363; Rorb logFC -0.9010 P=7.09e-05 FDR=0.4044; Lnpk logFC 0.3055 FDR=0.8137; Cacna2d3 logFC -0.4686 FDR=0.8137.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: The L4-5 IT cortical Rorb signature had the clearest target-transcript decrease but only nominally ranked downstream genes.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Pearson score correlations with Rorc were Rora r=0.007, Rorb r=0.009, Nr1d1 r=-0.046, and Nr1d2 r=-0.016. Across all shared cell types, the largest absolute Rorc correlation to Rora, Rorb, Nr1d1, or Nr1d2 was |r|=0.095.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: Rorc signatures were effectively uncorrelated with assayed ROR paralogs and REV-ERB neighbors.

evidence_ledger_rows.statistics: Clock set: 198 rows for Nr1d1, Nr1d2, Arntl, Clock, Cry1, Cry2, Per1, Per2, and Per3; minimum nominal p=0.018120 and minimum FDR=1.0. Metabolic/lipid set: 132 rows for Srebf1, Srebf2, Cyp51, Apoe, Sult4a1, and Cyp46a1; minimum nominal p=0.012651 and minimum FDR=1.0.
evidence_ledger_rows.description: Genes representing RORE-linked clock and lipid/steroid metabolism functions showed only unadjusted, uncoordinated tails after Rorc perturbation.

caveats: Rora touched only a narrow clock-linked branch, so the phenotype is not a full circadian oscillator collapse.
Rorb and Rorc were weakly engaged, making paralog non-interchangeability suggestive rather than a clean knockout comparison.
